findings.title: Cleanup ticker shortened from 10 minutes to 1 minute for all jobs
findings.body: The ticker interval was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, but this ticker drives CleanUpService.clean(), which runs every cleanup job (expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, and query history), not just annotation cleanup. Nothing in the PR description justifies a 10x increase in frequency for all of these jobs. This will increase database and filesystem load on every Grafana instance and shorten the effective timeout/interference window between full cleanup passes; it looks like a leftover local-testing change and should be reverted or scoped/justified separately.

findings.title: Routine cleanup batches are logged at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log every batch at Error level (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), including on success paths where err is nil, and they include the complete ids slice and SQL condition. With the configured batch size this can dump tens of thousands of IDs into error logs once per batch until cleanup finishes, creating false error alerts/on-call noise, high log volume and serialization cost, and obscuring real failures. These progress messages should be Debug (or Info without the ID list), with Error reserved for the returned error path.

findings.title: Placeholder-limit workaround only handles SQLite and keys off configured batch size
findings.body: deleteByIDs inlines IDs only when the database is SQLite and cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999; otherwise it emits one '?' placeholder per ID. PostgreSQL and MySQL also have bind-parameter limits (65535), so a user who raises annotation_cleanupjob_batchsize above that (the new test itself encourages very large batches such as 32767) will now get 'too many parameters' failures from the DELETE and cleanup will error on every cycle, whereas the previous subquery DELETE had no host-parameter limit. The guard should be based on len(ids) and the actual dialect's parameter limit, chunking or inlining as needed per database.
